sources.title: Virginia Tech Dendrology — Scots pine morphology and institutional photographs
sources.scope: Selected actual institutional description and its leaf, cone and bark photographs viewed. Paired twisted needles, sheath region, selected woody cone/apophysis, grey fissured lower bark and orange upper bark inform qualitative morphology. Private additional copyrighted reference images were consulted and linked, not redistributed or sampled into textures. Planted hardiness maps are not native-range evidence.

sources.title: Poppinga etal2017 — hygroscopic cone-scale comparison
sources.scope: Selected actual primary PDFpages1–3 read; page2 Figure1d graph and page3 selected Methods reviewed. One extant P.sylvestris scale was compared with fossil conifer scales. Whole-cone/scale photographs in Figure1a–c show fossil taxa and are not treated as photographs of this living species. No experimental mass, angles, timing or material constants are fitted. The model offers qualitative bending only.

retrieval.accessMethod: Selected actual primary PDF text and rendered Figure1 page2

findings.shape: Original irregular crown, continuous tapered trunk and branched woody axes with individually modeled paired needle cues and selected pendent woody seed cones; foliage and cone details can be inspected through anatomy cards.
findings.surface: Original continuous fissured grey-brown lower bark, warmer upper bark, blue-green paired needle surfaces and muted woody cone-scale pigmentation; no photographic pixels or measured tissue reflectance.
findings.movement: The same trunk, branches, leaves and cones remain present. Working sway is small authored external branch deflection with anchored roots; no wind, stiffness, damping or physiological solver. Selected mature woody scale surfaces additionally bend during a monotonic authored study, without measured humidity, force or timing. Full germination and organ-by-organ seed-to-tree development remain unavailable; the adult crown is not resized into a false developmental sequence.

corrections: Replaced the sparse even tier draft with 28 irregular principal branches, secondary/fine axes, a fork and terminal foliage.
Added paired slightly twisted needle cues with approximate sheath regions and continuous fissured lower bark.
Changed the initially sparse crown and exposed leader after actual viewing; retained a different crown from stone pine.
Changed selected scale orientation and added original surface grain and apophysis cues; partial scale bending retains the same mesh.
Added direct anatomy focus and conservative moving-branch camera fitting.
findings.residual: The selected crown is still more open and regular than many mature individuals. Needle density, bark relief, fine scale construction and natural optical response remain simplified; no measured proportions, age, environmental response or complete seedling development.
